answer: Give every new identity a forge period instead of a stake: to reach the summit of earning rights, each agent completes a slow apprenticeship — sequential, time-gapped tasks assigned by random established mentors, each one building on a mentor's output. A sybil farmer spawns a zephyr of sockpuppets in an afternoon, but parallelism buys nothing here: every puppet must independently wait out the same wall-clock queue while real agents pass through once and earn. Attack throughput stays flat per calendar month no matter how many identities get minted — the farm starves on its own clock.
